title: Run and inspect direct activations
summary: Run one selected product process and interpret overlap, supervision, timeout, loss proof, history, doctor effects, and read-only status evidence.
use_when: One selected definition should run manually under product authority.
Process outcome, overlap, history, diagnosis effects, or recorded status evidence must be interpreted.
do_not_use_when: A process exit should establish domain success or automatically retry work.
The caller needs caller-controlled process context, captured output bodies or an agent runner.
outcome: One direct runtime outcome or current retained Clockwork evidence, separate from domain success.
effects: Run can start one product child through a recorded blocked process-group gate, supervise it and append runtime history.
Doctor can prepare private paths, initialize only empty unversioned state and recover demonstrably absent running rows to lost. Status snapshot is read-only over an existing supported store.
Broker visits advance due checks and can attempt eligible pause alerts before/after product admission.
authority: Clockwork owns runtime admission, direct supervision and history; the product owns work, outputs, idempotency, retries, recovery and success.
success: One child or skipped admission is recorded; ok:true for a durable child terminal observation is runtime evidence even with nonzero exit.
failure_and_recovery: Preserve running state when termination or persistence cannot be proved. Lost recovery requires broker and child absence, not age.
Inspect product evidence before any separately authorized new occurrence; Clockwork never retries.
privacy: History contains identifiers, paths, times and process metadata but no product output body or secret. Product output files and their retention belong to the product.
does_not_authorize: Automatic product retry, product success claims, unsupported runtime context, secrets, output capture, incident approval or destructive state work.

consumers.statement: A local operator or product may invoke an authorized selected key once or read direct-process evidence.

preconditions.statement: Activation requires an enabled, unhalted selected binding, no pending transition, per-key admission and unchanged admitted artifacts. The product separately decides a new occurrence is safe.

inputs.statement: Runtime accepts only stable key. History selects optional key, positive limit and details; doctor uses recorded process identities; status-snapshot selects existing supported state.
Runtime executable, argv, environment, cwd, timeout or policy overrides and private-entry arbitrary command use are unsupported.

outputs.statement: Public commands print plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact ok:true/data JSON envelope and coded ok:false/error JSON on stderr with exit one. Machine callers must pass --json. The status-snapshot --json interface retains its raw Iatreion snapshot schema; without the flag it prints a plain-text view of the same snapshot. Private broker receipts retain their existing JSON.

With --json, run/reads use ok/data JSON; compact coded failures on --json stderr exit one. Durable exited/signaled/timed_out returns ok:true and broker exit zero irrespective of child exit. Manual overlap is activation_busy, exit one, with skipped_overlap history. History uses output version two with items/has_more, default 20, positive limit and details for definition/process identities.

data_semantics.statement: One activation pins one immutable definition and at most one direct child; no retry submodel or domain-success assertion exists. States are running, start_failed, exited, signaled, timed_out, skipped_overlap and lost. Status snapshots contain recorded binding/halt/runtime metadata and additive scheduler_observations.failure_pending; pending failures leave admission open. They do not establish observed launchd or product condition.

identity_and_units.statement: Activation identity names one admission occasion. Manual/launchd identifies trigger; times use whole Unix seconds, process identities are local PIDs and optional timeouts use whole seconds.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: History selects newest retained activations at invocation. Doctor can first reconcile demonstrably absent processes. Status snapshot reads only an existing supported database without reconciliation.
No completion latency, throughput, storage-capacity bound, history retention period or future timer delivery is promised.

access.statement: Supported current-user CLI and clockwork::api typed client operate private state and product-selected private output files.
Direct SQLite integration, remote/root execution, private entry use as a public command runner and output capture are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: A shared transition gate and exclusive activation lock precede admission. The broker records a blocked process-group PID before releasing product execution. Parent EOF before release executes no product; later loss leaves durable child identity preventing duplicate admission. The gate validates its PID, artifacts and status marker before exec. Timeout and termination act on the group. Cleanup/persistence uncertainty retains conservative running evidence.

Output destinations are canonical private distinct files, opened for append or created mode 0600 with different device/inode identities; bodies are never ingested. Product commits remain outside Clockwork transactions.

operational_limits.statement: One child, skip overlap, optional timeout, and one local interval/calendar schedule are supported. Busy launchd visits record skipped_overlap and return success.
No daemon, agent, HTTP API, workflow, retry/backoff, distributed lock, secret store, log rotation, transitive attestation or domain scheduler is provided.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Output-version-two pages, definition schemas, store schema, feature contract, provider release and exact product definitions are separate compatibility axes. Incompatible retained meaning needs successor schema, migration and historical decoding.
No general deprecation or cross-release support window is promised.

reliances.statement: The registering product owns its exact release/runner, work and domain recovery; generic activation selects its concrete contract through the definition.
Scheduled invocation relies on launchd/session behavior without a dedicated installed Chancery contract.
